newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - July 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

On a visit to the West Australian mining town of Kalgoorlie on Monday, Prime Minister John Howard is expected to announce the Federal Government is dropping plans to cap the diesel fuel rebate for the mining industry. The decision should appease those inthe mining industry affected by the government's handling of the Reserve Bank gold sell-off. Page 1.

In a move that signifies a relaxation in its opposition to takeovers of regional banks, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission will allow Westpac Banking Corp to go ahead with its A$1.44 billion takeover bid for the Bank of Melbourne on the codition that Westpac must give deposit-taking institutions access to its electronic banking network in Victoria at reasonable rates. Page 1.

In a move that will affect the tense negotiations between the Gorgon partners and the North-West Shelf joint venture, Mobil Oil is planning a six million-tonne-a-year floating liquefied natural gas plant over the Gorgon gas field on the North-West Shelf. The plan follows similar ideas by both BHP Petroleum and Shell. Page 35.

The board of Foster's Brewing Group is expected to reduce its board following shareholder approval of a A$625 million buyback of its own stock from Asahi Breweries of Japan. The buyback unwinds the 51 percent holding in Foster's of Asahi and BHP and will invove the departure of three BHP and two Asahi representatives from the board. Page 35.

Australian Investment Managers' Association chair, corporate governance, Ian Horton said yesterday there should be a new format in company reports that will allow for more details of executive remuneration. Horton said AIMA members will continue to push or further disclosure of information. Page 35.

The announcement of the merger between Australis Media Ltd and Foxtel, a joint venture between Telstra and News Corporation, is expected to be announced next week as the Foxtel partners work on the logistics of the merger and redraft some contracts. The merger will be a key step in rationalising Australia's loss-making pay-TV industry. Page 35.
THE AUSTRALIAN

National Australia Bank chief executive Don Argus said yesterday the bank, which lost A$650 million off its market capitalisation following the release of a lower than expected June quarter profit of A$504 million, would need to increase fee income and cut costs to improve returns on its domestic operations. Page 25.

While economists agreed yesterday that the release of figures showing the smallest quarterly wages growth in almost four years, along with Wednesday's figures showing low inflation figures, indicates the economy is running below capacity and inflation wasnot a threat, they were divided over whether the Reserve Bank will today make another interest rate cut. Page 25.

The launch of new independent grocery retailer FoodWorks Supermarket Group, which has struck a supply agreement with Woolworth's Australian Independent Wholesalers, should break the monopoly on the market held by Davids, and gives Woolworths a foot in thedoor in the independent grocery market. Page 25.

Airspace 2000, a redesign of Australian skies undertaken by Dick Smith and representatives from the Civil Aviation Safety Authority and Airservices Australia, is causing some emotive debate. While Airservices has approved the plan, CASA is taking a little longer to make up its mind, a delay troubling Smith, who says the plan must be approved by its scheduled starting date of December 4. Page 27.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, which now regulates the telecommunications sector, has forced one of the new players into the industry, AAPT, to amend its advertising on the grounds that it is misleading and deceptive. The ACCC said AAPT advertised its long distance rates were charged at a single flat rate, yet they were in fact peak, off peak and economy rates for STD calls. Page 27.

Aristocrat Leisure Industries and the Australian Stock Exchange were locked in negotiations last night in an attempt to find a compromise on the ASX's demand for the release of fresh information on serious allegations against Aristocrat by the Colorado Gaming Control Commission. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The National Australia Bank lost A$650 million off its value yesterday as investors reacted to their third-quarter results, which showed the bank's aggressive push for market share had not succeeded. Earnings for the June quarter dropped by A$1 million t A$504 million compared to the same period last year. Page 25.

Financial planners say retirees and those people reaching retirement face complex choices to ensure an adequate income during their retirement as the financial environment becomes one of interest rate cuts and low inflation. Self-funded retirees are being hit by interest rate cuts, with an average A$350 a year being lost for every A$10,000 invested in bank accounts. Page 25.

Market traders are warning the Australian dollar could fall below the 73 U.S. cent mark as the foreign exchange market interpreted yesterday's figures showing lower than expected average weekly ordinary time earnings figures as a guarantee that the Reserve Bank will cut interest rates. Page 25.

Lend Lease remains a sole bidder in the battle for the A$200 million Docklands Stadium in Melbourne following the withdrawal of Hudson Conway from the bidding process for unspecified reasons. The withdrawal affects Kerry Packer, who had an interest in th Lend Lease-Hudson Conway consortium through his 20 percent share of Hudson Conway. Page 25.

HSBC Capel research analyst Chris Bedingfield said yesterday that investors in Australia's A$19.4 billion listed property trust sector already may have made their profits, with prices probably already peaking. Bedingfield told a Property Council seminar yesterday that prices may not go higher as property trust investors had driven up unit prices to a strong premium to the underlying valuation of their assets. Page 27.

The Grollo group yesterday confirmed that it had reached a settlement with the Australian Tax Office following a Federal Court judgment handed down earlier in the year. The full court of the Federal Court found that half the A$59 million the tax office claimed was owed on revenue from the Rialto building project should be paid. Page 27.
THE AGE

The National Australia Bank reported a A$1,643 million profit for the nine months to June, an increase of 9.3 percent over the same period last year, yet all the growth was achieved in the first two quarters, with profit for the June quarter A$54 million, down A$1 million on last year. Page B1.

Acacia Resources yesterday shrugged off the gloom in the gold industry when it announced record production and profits for the June quarter. The gold producer's share price closed a cent up after announcing its profit before abnormals for the June half was expected to be about A$13 million, up from A$7.5 million in the same period last year. Page B3.

After the release of the industry-support report, the Mortimer Report, the textile, clothing and footwear sector could play an important part in the policy debate. The sector is under scrutiny from the Industry Commission, which has recommended tariff cuts. Page B3.

David Syme managing director John Reynolds will leave the John Fairfax owned publisher to take up the newly-created position of group executive, strategy and structure, with Normandy Mining. It is expected Reynolds will strengthen Normandy's management of human resources. Page B3.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission head Professor Allan Fels said the regulator would be cracking down on telecommunications companies after it yesterday forced AAP Telecommunications to correct some misleading advertising just weeks after entering the deregulated market. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
